text: The passage repays attention to what is missing. Sarah appears nowhere in Genesis 22; the book reports her death in the verse that immediately follows it. The scene implies, without direct statement, that something in the household did not survive the mountain. Abraham returns to the servants, and Isaac is no longer named there. At the very point where a weaker story would have detained itself, the narration leaves the matter; such silence conveys meaning, and does more than leave out Sarah and Isaac.
